RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Question s for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, the July 15, 2002/Asadha 24, 1924 (Saka)
————
(Ministries:  Development of North Eastern Region; Disinvestment; Health and
Family Welfare; Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Information
 and Broadcasting; Law and Justice; Shipping;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Urban
Development and Poverty Alleviation)
Total number of questions—20
1
FDI in print media
*1. SHRI ABANI ROY:
DR. ABRAR AHMED:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to allow 26 per cent foreign direct investment
in print media inspite of stiff opposition;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the small and medium
newspaper industry in the country is likely
to suffer a lot due to this decision; and
(d) if so, the steps Government are going
to take to protect them?
Disinvestment of PSUs
*2. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of public
undertakings under various Ministries,
Ministry-wise;
(b) the total number of PSUs in respect
of which decision has been taken to
disinvest them and proceeds realized after
completing the process of disinvestment/
sale;
(c) the number of PSUs in respect of
which a decision has been taken to disinvest
but the process not yet completed/proceeds
not yet realized after the sale/disinvestment;
and
(d) the number of PSUs still with
Government and the steps taken to improve
their management and functioning?
Disposal of surplus land of VSNL
*3. SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
floating a separate company to dispose of
surplus land available with the VSNL;
(b) whether any agreement has been
reached with the new management of
VSNL;
(c) whether permission to float a new
company will have to be taken from US
Securities and Exchange Commission; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

National Judicial Commission
*4. SHRI C.P. THIRUNAVUKKA-
RASU: Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to form a National Judicial Commission for
making appointments in Judiciary; and
(b) if so, by when it will be formed?
Bifurcation of National Commission
for SCs and STs
*5. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
bifurcate the National Commission for
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes;
and
(b) if so, the reasons therefor?
Increase in seats in Dental and Medical
Colleges
*6. SHRI JIBON ROY: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned,
"Admissions: 76 Dental, Medical Colleges
out", which appeared in the Indian Express
dated the 17th June, 2002; and
(b) if so, what steps Government have
taken to increase seats in Dental and
Medical Colleges so that students do not
suffer because of malafide intentions of
some Private/Government Medical
Colleges?
Absentee doctors in AIIMS
†*7. SHRI RAMA SHANKER
KAUSHIK: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) since when senior doctors of various
important departments of AIIMS have been
absent;
(b) the number of such absentees along
with the names of their respective
departments and whether it is a fact that all
facilities including job, accommodation,
telephone to such absentee doctors have not
only been continuing but they have been
given promotions also;
(c) the reasons for not taking any action
against the said doctors; and
(d) the payments made by Government,
so far, to the said doctors and the action
Government would take to terminate their
services and to recover the said payments
from them?
Research work at AIIMS
*8. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned,
"Research work at AIIMS being hampered
for want of animals", which appeared in the
Hindustan Times, dated the 11th June, 2002;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto; and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to
address the problems highlighted by the
news-item which are hampering the medical
research at AIIMS?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Collection of property tax from
Central Government assets
*9. SHRI PRASANTA CHATTER-
JEE: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have agreed, in principle, to allow the local
bodies to collect property tax in respect of
Central Government assets; and
(b) if so, the latest position in this regard?
Investment of VSNL capital in Tata
Teleservices
*10. SHRI NILOTP

List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS

(Ministries:  Development of North-Eastern Region; Disinvestment; Health

Total number of questions—51
1
News-item "Disinvestment train on
slow track"
1. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned,
"Disinvestment train on slow track", which
appeared in the Business Standard dated
13th June, 2002;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to
address the problems responsible for the
slow-down of the disinvestment process as
highlighted in the news-item?
Disinvestment of PSUs
2. SHRI BHAGATRAM MANHAR:
SHRI RAJU PARMAR:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to disinvest National Fertilizers Limited
(NFL);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have decided
to disinvest PSUs like EIL, BEML, RCF,
NALCO, Neyveli Lignite Corporation and
STC Limited; and
(d) if so, the latest position with regard
to disinvestment of these PSUs, Company-
wise?
Demonstration by CGHS employees
3. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Central Government
Health Scheme employees held a
demonstration on the 19th, June 2002 in
support of their demands in New Delhi;
(b) whether the recommendations of the
Fifth Pay Commission concerning these
employees have not been implemented;
and
(c) Government's response to their
demands?

CAG report on National Programme
for Control of Blindness
4. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Comptroller and Auditor
General of India has criticized Government
for poor implementation of National
Programme for Control of Blindness;
(b) if so, whether according to the report
placed before the Parliament, it has pointed
out that more than 70 lakh prospective
beneficiaries were left untargeted;
(c) if so, the main reasons for not
implementing the National Programme for
Blindness; and
(d) the measures Government propose
to take to implement fully the project for
removing blindness in the country?
National Health Policy
5. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRI NANA DESHMUKH:
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
announced the new National Health Policy;
(b) if so, whether Government propose
that two years' of rural posting would be
mandatory for medical graduates and would
be done through the Medical Council;
(c) if so, the other main features of the
policy; and
(d) the steps being taken to implement
them?
Winding up of CGHS dispensaries
6. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
wind up CGHS dispensaries in congested
localities as several local doctors are available
for consultation and restrict dispensaries
to far-flung areas only where doctors are
not available, especially in rural areas;
(b) if so, the details of plans made in this
regard; and
(c) if not, how health care of people will
be taken care of in far-flung rural
areas?
Supply of oxygen in Kalavati Saran
Children's Hospital
†7. SHRI RAMA SHANKER
KAUSHIK: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether an attempt to kill dozens of
new born babies/child patients was made
by stopping supply of oxygen on the 1st
June, 2002 in Kalavati Saran Children's
Hospital;
(b) whether Government have taken any
action against the culprits after making
inquiries into the incident of shutting off the
oxygen plant;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government have ensured
that the parents of the hospitalized children
remain free from fear and such incident does
not recur in future; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Options to CGHS beneficiaries
8. DR. ALLADI  P. RAJKUMAR: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
consider giving options to CGHS
beneficiaries to consult reputed doctors
locally and purchase medicines direct instead
of visiting CGHS dispensaries where
medicines prescribed are not available and
doctors generally are not in their seats;
(b) if so, the plans made in this regard;
and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Working of CGHS dispensaries
